hero.headline: A dental CAD built native, from the ground up.
hero.subhead: DentalCraft is a desktop application for digital dentistry, written in Rust with a GPU 3D viewport. It starts with clear aligner planning and is designed to grow module by module.
hero.microcopy: Early stage. Linux and Windows first. Made in Italy.

presentation.label: Presentation
presentation.headline: What DentalCraft is, and where it stands
presentation.body.1: DentalCraft is a native dental CAD. It grows out of an orthodontic aligner planning tool that its author first built as a Blender add-on. DentalCraft rebuilds that work as a dedicated, faster, standalone application, with a structure inspired by professional dental CAD suites: a common core plus modules.
presentation.body.2: The project is at an early stage. Today the application shell, the project format and the 3D viewport exist. Scan import and the clinical algorithms are being ported and validated.

vision.label: Vision
vision.banner: What follows is intent, not a description of finished features.
vision.headline: Why a native dental CAD
vision.body: Dental planning means heavy 3D data and long sessions. We think the software should stay fast, stay local and stay under the clinician's control. DentalCraft is being built around those ideas.
vision.p1.title: Native performance.
vision.p1.body: A Rust application with a GPU (wgpu / Vulkan) viewport. The aim: no UI freezes, even with large scans.
vision.p2.title: Offline-first.
vision.p2.body: Projects live on your machine. The software should not need a connection to do its work.
vision.p3.title: One open project file.
vision.p3.body: A single documented .dcprj file: a versioned ZIP container with checksums.
vision.p4.title: Pseudonymised patient data.
vision.p4.body: Project files are designed to carry no patient names.
vision.p5.title: English and Italian interface.
vision.p6.title: Linux and Windows first.
vision.p7.title: Built with a regulatory mindset.
vision.p7.body: Requirements, risk management and traceability are carried over from day one.
vision.p8.title: Independent and made in Italy.
vision.microcopy: These are design intentions. They describe where we are heading.
roadmap.label: Roadmap
roadmap.headline: One core, several modules
roadmap.body: DentalCraft is structured as a common core with modules on top. Aligners comes first. The others are planned, with no dates.

aligners.label: Aligners
aligners.headline: From scan to aligner, in one workspace
aligners.body: The Aligners module is designed to follow the clinical path from intraoral scan to printable output. The stages below are grouped like the application menu.
aligners.banner: Intended workflow. Each stage is tagged Planned or In progress. Nothing here is available yet.
aligners.s2.micro: Make the data ready to plan.
aligners.s2.stages: Orientation and arch; FDI tooth numbering; segmentation; tooth reconstruction and gingiva
aligners.s3.stages: Space analysis; Little irregularity index; Bolton analysis
aligners.s4.micro: Define the target and the steps.
aligners.s4.stages: Setup of the final position; staging per aligner with per-tooth movement limits; IPR; attachments
aligners.s5.stages: Occlusion and bite, including bite with aligners
aligners.s6.stages: Aligner shell with thickness and clearance; trim line; identification stamp; print check

technology.label: Technology
technology.headline: Native code, local data
technology.body: Technical choices that serve speed, control and traceability.
technology.i1.title: Rust, native desktop.
technology.i1.body: One compiled application. No browser engine in the middle.
technology.i2.title: GPU viewport.
technology.i2.body: 3D rendering through wgpu on Vulkan, for smooth handling of dense meshes.
technology.i3.title: Open project file (.dcprj).
technology.i3.body: A ZIP container with checksums, versioned and documented.
technology.i4.title: Privacy by design.
technology.i4.body: Patient data is pseudonymised: no names in project files.
technology.i5.title: Offline-first.
technology.i5.body: Work on local projects. An account (auth.dentalcraft.app) is planned for licences and support only.
technology.i6.title: Bilingual UI.
technology.microcopy: Details will be published as the project format stabilises.
regulatory.label: Regulatory
regulatory.headline: Honest about where we are
regulatory.callout: In development. Not a medical device. Not for clinical use.
regulatory.body.1: DentalCraft is not a medical device and is not certified. It must not be used for clinical purposes.
regulatory.body.2: The project is being built with a regulatory mindset: requirements, risk management and traceability are carried over from the earlier work. The intention is to pursue the appropriate medical-device conformity path when the software is ready for it. That is an intention, not a status.
faq.label: FAQ
faq.headline: Questions, answered plainly
faq.a1: Not yet. It is in early development. The application shell, project format and 3D viewport exist. Scan import and the clinical algorithms are being ported and validated.
faq.q2: Is it certified? Is it a medical device?
faq.a2: No. DentalCraft is not a medical device and holds no certification. It is not for clinical use. We are building with a regulatory mindset and intend to pursue the appropriate conformity path in the future.
faq.q3: Which platforms will it run on?
faq.a3: Linux and Windows first. macOS later.
faq.a5: The design is offline-first: projects stay on your machine. Project files are pseudonymised and carry no patient names. An account is planned only for licences and support.
faq.a6: Not yet. Early access is planned for later. Come back to this site for news.
faq.a7: The first module is Aligners, for clear aligner planning. The intended workflow is described above; it is being ported and validated, and nothing in it is available yet.
faq.q8: Which file formats does it use?
faq.a8: Scans in STL, OBJ and PLY are intended as inputs. Projects use a single open .dcprj file. Per-stage export is intended as STL.
contact.label: Contact
privacy.label: Privacy
privacy.headline: No cookies, no tracking, no forms
privacy.body.1: This website sets no cookies, runs no analytics or tracking scripts, loads nothing from third parties and has no forms. We do not collect personal data through it. Your language choice is kept only in your own browser, so that the site can open in your language next time.
privacy.body.2: Like any web server, the one hosting this site may keep standard access logs (IP address, time, page requested) for security and troubleshooting. If you write to hello@dentalcraft.app, we use your message only to reply.
